newsitem.title: UK: Stg/mark mired after falling on central bank worry. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Stg/mark mired after falling on central bank worry. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]

text.p: Sterling hovered above lows it set amid unconfirmed talk the Bank of England sold (corrects from bought) pounds.

The pound slumped 0.5 percent against the mark after speculation of UK central bank intervention surfaced. Traders said talk that one or two other European central banks bought marks also contributed to the German currency's gains.
The Bank of England declined to comment on the talk and traders grew more sceptical about whether it had intervened.
Still, sterling remained mired near the session's lows amid expectations it is due for a deeper correction after setting an 80-month high of 3.0327 marks on Monday.

"There were rumours that the Old Lady was in but I do not think this was likely," said Harry Quaderer, chief trader at Westdeutsche Landesbank in London. "Sterling is still in an uptrend, but people are looking for a correction."

Sterling was at 3.0053/63 at 0835 GMT from 3.0105/15 late Wednesday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6730/40 from $1.6744/49 yesterday. The pound's trade-weighted index was down at 104.8 from Wednesday's close of 105.2.
The pound has soared more than 11 percent so far this year against a trade-weighted basket of 20 currencies, climbing to its highest levels in nearly seven years.
While this has eroded UK exporters' competitiveness and the value of their foreign-currency earnings, it has not yet had a dramatic impact on trade data.
Traders are also not expecting the Bank of England to step in to halt the pound's rally anytime soon as they will be fighting against the weight of economic fundamentals.
"I would not expect them to intervene as this would give the market a target to go for," said Quaderer at Westdeutsche Landesbank.
Expectations of higher UK interest rates have already boosted sterling five percent against the mark so far this month.
They are expected by analysts to limit sterling's losses in the coming days.

"The ongoing interest-rate argument will help to underpin sterling," said Tim Fox, treasury analyst at Standard Chartered. Sterling/mark "is close to the top but it is still a little early to call an end to its rally".
